Emily — thanks, heard loud and clear. Attaching the CSV and the math; below is the short readout and proposed acceptance criteria.

Quick readout (summary):
- Target slab: 8 x A100-80GB-equivalent (mixed-precision) GPUs dedicated to Helix (isolated lane).
- Guaranteed serving envelope (per-slab): 3.6k p50 tokens/s and 850 p95 tokens/s for sequence length median 256; equivalent to ~140 QPS for 32-token generation latency p95 goal of 1200ms.
- Warm-pool: keep 2 GPUs (25% of slab) as hot-standby with KV cache primed for top-10 models. Cold-start penalty measured at +420–650ms depending on model; warmup amortized to <150ms after cache priming.
- Admission control: soft admission at 80% slab utilization, hard reject at 94% sustained utilization over a 30s sliding window. Expected reject-rate under modeled 99th-percentile traffic spike ~1.2% (see CSV sim).
- Egress: plan for 220 MB/s per slab peak (includes streaming overhead + telemetry). Recommend VPC peering baseline across two 10Gbps links for redundancy.

Acceptance criteria (what Helix signs off on):
1) Measured p95 generation latency <= 1200ms for 32-token median case across 72-hour soak at committed QPS.
2) Failover to fallback model (quantized 4-bit) occurs <500ms when slab falls under emergency threshold (operator trigger).
3) Rejection rate during synthetic 99th spike <= 2.5% (we target 1.2%).
4) Network egress sustained <= 220 MB/s during peak sustained windows; sustained over 10 minutes triggers auto-throttle.

Attachments: lane-slab-simulation-20281004.csv (detailed simulation trace), carveout-sizing-math.xlsx, warm-pool-warmup-profiles.pdf

I'll have Jonas add the simulation notes below, and Laura can confirm the contractual language.

Emily / Vanessa — dropping the simulation notes and a few knobs to tune the headroom math. Key items from the run:

Summary of simulation inputs (see CSV):
- Traffic model: production trace from a 6-week window (sampled), scaled to Helix target commit of 100 QPS steady, with fat-tail bursts up to 650 QPS for <90s durations.
- Model mix: 65% small chat-style (64 tokens), 35% long-form (512 tokens) — we simulated both MV and KV caching scenarios.
- Hardware: A100-80 equivalency; NVLink assumed inside slab for KV-sharing; per-GPU batching hard cap of 48 sequences.

Findings:
- With 8 GPUs (slab) and 2-GPU warm pool: steady 100 QPS p95 latency = 980ms (small chat), long-form p95 ~ 1.05s; p50s are sub-200ms for small chat.
- Under the fat-tail 650 QPS spike, admission-control triggered and kept latency p95 below 3s by shedding at 94% utilization; observed reject-rate ~1.16% (aligned with Vanessa summary).
- Cache priming (warm-pool) reduces cold-start penalty by ~60% for heavy KV models; warm-pool hit-rate depends on request locality — we recommend a 72-hour rolling priming window for your top-20 prompts to keep hit-rate > 68%.

Tunable levers we recommend for negotiation: 
1) Increase warm-pool to 3 GPUs (37.5%) if Helix expects >25% long-form traffic — reduces p95 worst-case by ~210ms at cost of reserved capacity.
2) Enable continuous batching with a 40ms dispatch window for small-chat peaks — gives a ~12% token-cost saving without materially increasing tail latency.
3) Set the soft admission at 75% if you want earlier throttling and lower rejection variance (trades off utilization).

I've attached the raw CSV trace (lane-slab-simulation-20281004.csv) with per-second utilization, queue depth, and rejected-counts. Happy to walk through offline.

— Jonas

Emily — quick note on contract language we propose to make these acceptance criteria actionable for procurement:

1) Performance SLA: Redwood will warrant (during the 30-day acceptance period) that p95 generation latency for a 32-token median workload will be <= 1200ms when measured over 72 hours of live traffic at the committed QPS. Failure to meet this allows Helix a single remediation window (30 days) for configuration changes; if unresolved, Helix may elect a pro-rata credit for the first 90 days.

2) Rejection/Admission: The agreement will define soft admission (advisory) at 75% and hard admission at 94% sustained over 30s. Rejection-rate thresholds used for acceptance will be the modeled 99th percentile surge test; target <= 2.5%.

3) Warm-pool baseline: Redwood will provision 2 GPUs as warm-pool by default, and provide a documented warmup profile. If Helix requires a 3-GPU warm-pool, that will be priced as an additional reserved unit.

4) Network: Redwood provides guidance for egress ceilings; Helix is responsible for peerings/BGP. If observed sustained egress > agreed ceiling due to known Redwood behavior, parties will negotiate mitigation credits.

I'll send a short redline tomorrow with the exact credit language. For now, confirm you accept the numeric thresholds and I will trigger SOW drafting.

Thanks,
